passage:
"Miss Sharmila, Rohan says I took his crayon and I didn't!" said Mahima, her fists tight.
"Tell me what happened," said Miss Sharmila.
"He told everybody I did. I was so angry. And it hurt my tummy. I thought he was my friend."
"I'm glad you came to me. Let's look in his box together."
The red crayon was in Rohan's own pencil case. "Oh," Rohan mumbled.
Later he said, "Sorry, Mahima."
Mahima frowned. "Don't say it again."

qa.a: The red crayon was in Rohan's own pencil case.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when Rohan told everybody she took his crayon?
qa.a: Mahima felt angry, hurt and confused. She had thought Rohan was her friend, so being blamed made her tummy hurt.

qa.q: Which choice by Mahima worked, and what could help the two children afterwards?
qa.a: She went to the teacher and told what really happened. If Rohan keeps his sorry and does not do it again, their friendship may recover.

qa.q: How might Rohan have felt when the crayon was found in his pencil case?
qa.a: Rohan was probably embarrassed and maybe worried about being in trouble. His mumbled "Oh" suggests he knew he had been wrong.

grounding: A friend lies and says the child took his crayon, she feels angry, hurt and confused, tells a teacher what really happened, and a sorry may repair the friendship.
